data.name: Flute Master
data.detailed_description:
Is playing recorder always the same? Is it not exciting? Well, that's different with Flute Master! Here you will learn to play soprano recorder while experiencing a great adventure in the world of music.

Everyone can learn it! The notes you play will be detected over the device's microphone. Just install it and start right away!

Please Note:
⚠ Flute Master requires a real recorder (the flute instrument)!
⚠ Use headphones if you can. This helps the game listen only to your recorder.


In Flute Master, you and Oratio will help the dragon Cornelius protect his tower of strawberries from the greedy bats. Yes, in the World of Music, bats love strawberries!

You'll play a lot of unique music tracks that gradually teach you each note on your recorder. By the time you finish the game, you'll be able to play great recorder tunes! ;)

Try to score as high as you can and... scare away those bats!


Features:
✔ Game-based learning to introduce you to the recorder.
✔ Real-time detection of the instrument, using your microphone.
✔ 27 original music tracks composed by music education professionals.
✔ Available in several languages: English, German, Spanish, French and Portuguese (PT and BR).
✔ Interactive learning system for recorder fingering positions, music theory and sheet music reading.
✔ Notes associated with colours, for easier recognition.
✔ A scoring system that encourages self-improvement.
✔ An amusing story with cute characters
✔ Ready for classroom use.


Flute Master is part of the Classplash Music series and focuses on teaching the basics of recorder flute by gradually introducing each note in a game environment, showing correct recorder fingering positions and providing music sheets for all tracks.

Teachers can use Flute Master to great effect during classes. By teaching through gaming, especially kids, it increases their engagement and makes the learning experience much more productive!

Does the content follow the music curriculum?

Yes! And even primary school teachers without a musical background can use it in the classroom. It's the result of a worldwide awarded project, which was developed with the collaboration of over 200 primary school students.


Q: Why is it called Flute Master if it teaches the recorder?
A: In some European countries - namely Portugal, where Classplash was born - "flute" (flauta) refers to the recorder flute. Only when talking about other flutes do we specify the type of flute (ex: transverse flute). This felt easier to understand for some non-english languages. In addition, "Recorder Master" was taken. ;)

reviews.review:
I bought this in the groupees bundle after it had been on my wishlist for a long time.  I haven't played any instruments since the 5th grade, which was about 35 years ago!  So I wanted to get into music as something else to do besides video games and work (really!).  I am a mix of several celtic ancestries so the bagpipes, bodhran, and tinwhistle/penny flute are of interest to me.  The flute was by far the cheapest to buy, even cheaper than a recorder.  So a while back I bought a book and I played a bit and can play a couple of tunes, but now I am trying a mix of gaming and music and I really like it.  The game interface is easy, and with a decent headset with mic you can play.  I play a C tinwhistle and it works fine.  The software is picking it up with nearly perfect accuracy, which is good since my notes are far from perfect.


The game is aimed clearly at elementary kids; as a grown up don't let that dissuade you because it is a good time very releaxing, though each level ups the challenge quite a bit.  I played alot of RockBand on Wii years ago, and it is like the level progression there...  ramps up quick.  Level 1 is just one note, level 2 is two, etc. presumably until you are playing all six notes on a recorder / pennywhistle.  I can only assume that it then goes into half notes (which I struggle with) and more complicated melodies, fingering, and breathing techniques.  I look forward to it!

So if you like the idea of rocksmith and don't want to go buy a guitar and cable, get this and a recorder or flute for the price of just the cable for rocksmith and see if these kinds of music progression games are your thing.  This is a real instrument and you will see real notes as you progress, not a game pad like Rockband has (though I loved those games!).

10/10 for 20cents in a bundle, and I think it would be 5/10 at full price as there are 30 tunes in 10 levels to keep you busy for 10+ hours.
